blocks.alt: Commercial Truck Wrap in Toronto: Apex Property Management's GMC Sierra Gets a Bold Partial Wrap

blocks.html:
Commercial truck wrap projects don’t always mean covering an entire vehicle. Sometimes a partial wrap paired with clean lettering makes a bigger impression for a smaller budget — and that’s exactly the route we took for Apex Property Management on their GMC Sierra. The result is a factory-black pickup that reads as confident, corporate, and unmistakably theirs from half a block away, here in Toronto and right across the GTA.

The Brief: Sharp Branding on a Factory-Black GMC Sierra

Apex Property Management wanted their GMC Sierra to look like a natural extension of their brand — professional enough to sit outside a condo board meeting, bold enough to get noticed on the road. The truck’s factory black paint was already a strong starting point, so a full colour change wasn’t needed. Instead, we designed printed graphics that use the existing black as negative space.

The design features:

  • A blue architectural skyline graphic that sweeps across the bed and cab, echoing the buildings Apex manages
  • Crisp white and blue truck lettering and decals for the website (apex1call.ca) and phone number
  • “Enforcement Unit” call-outs along the doors for their patrol vehicles
  • The Apex logo positioned for maximum visibility on both sides

Because the artwork sits on top of the OEM black, every element pops without competing for attention.

Why a Commercial Truck Wrap Made Sense Here

For a property management company, vehicles spend the day parked in visible, high-traffic spots — condo driveways, plaza lots, and residential streets across Etobicoke, Mississauga, Vaughan, and Brampton. That’s free advertising, but only if the vehicle is branded well.

A commercial truck wrap turns each of those parked hours into brand impressions. Compared with digital ads that stop the moment you stop paying, vinyl graphics are a one-time cost that keeps working for years.

Partial coverage made particular sense for Apex because it delivered:

  • Budget efficiency — a premium branded look without paying for full coverage
  • Speed — less material means faster turnaround and less vehicle downtime
  • Flexibility — decals and lettering are easy to update if contact details change
  • Protection — quality vinyl shields the panels it covers and removes cleanly

Partial Wrap vs. Full Wrap vs. Lettering: Choosing Your Coverage

One of the most common questions we hear from fleet managers is how much coverage they actually need. Here’s a simple comparison based on typical GTA market ranges:

Coverage LevelBest ForVisual ImpactEstimated GTA Range*Lettering & DecalsContact info, logos, complianceModerate$300 – $900Partial WrapBranded look on a budgetHigh$1,500 – $3,500Full WrapColour change + full brandingMaximum$3,500 – $6,500+

*General market estimates for reference only — not shop-confirmed pricing. Contact us for a free, exact quote on your vehicle.

For Apex, the partial wrap hit the sweet spot: near–full-wrap presence at a mid-range cost.

What a Job Like This Involves

A professional commercial truck wrap is far more than sticking vinyl on metal. Our process for the Sierra looked like this:

StageWhat HappensTypical TimeframeDesignConcept, revisions, print-ready proof2 – 4 business daysPrint & laminatePremium film printed and protected1 – 2 daysPrep & cleanPanels decontaminated for adhesionSame dayInstallationPrecision application, trimming, post-heating1 – 2 days

We use premium cast films from trusted manufacturers like 3M and Avery Dennison, backed by our 3-year warranty against peeling, bubbling, and fading. You can learn more about commercial films on 3M’s official vehicle graphics page.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Cheap vinyl — calendared films fade and lift within a season of Canadian winters. Cast vinyl is worth it.
  • Overcrowded design — too much text at highway speed reads as noise. White space sells.
  • DIY installation — bubbles, misalignment, and premature failure cost more than doing it right once.
  • Skipping the vector logo — low-resolution art prints blurry. Always supply a vector file.

The Result

Apex Property Management now runs a GMC Sierra that markets the company on every route it drives. This is a repeat relationship for us — we previously handled their Dodge Durango partial wrap — and consistent branding across a fleet builds recognition faster than any single vehicle could alone.

Ready to Wrap Your Truck?

If you’re a business owner or fleet manager in the GTA, a commercial truck wrap is one of the best-value marketing investments you can make in Ontario — and a proven advertising tool for businesses right across Canada. Whether you need a bold partial truck wrap, clean truck lettering and decals, or a full commercial vehicle wrap, our certified installers and in-house design team can bring it to life.

Call Vinyl Wrap Toronto at 416-746-1381, email info@VinylWrapToronto.com, or visit us at 24 Ronson Dr, Unit 1, Etobicoke, ON. Free estimates, fast turnaround, and a 3-year warranty on every wrap.

Frequently Asked Questions

  1. How much does a commercial truck wrap cost in Toronto?

    A partial truck wrap in the GTA typically runs between $1,500 and $3,500, while lettering and decals start lower and full wraps cost more. Final pricing depends on coverage, design complexity, and vehicle size. We provide free, exact quotes.

  2. How long does a truck wrap last?

    With premium cast vinyl and proper care, a quality wrap lasts five to seven years. Ours is backed by a 3-year warranty against peeling, bubbling, and fading.

  3. Will a wrap damage my truck’s paint?

    No. When professionally installed on sound factory paint and removed correctly, quality vinyl protects the surface underneath and comes off cleanly.

  4. Partial wrap or full wrap — which is better for my business?

    A partial wrap delivers most of the visual impact of a full wrap at a lower cost, making it ideal for companies that want strong branding on a budget. Full wraps suit colour changes and maximum coverage.

  5. How long does installation take?

    Most partial wraps and lettering jobs are completed within a few business days, including design time. Full wraps take longer.

  6. Do you serve areas outside Toronto?

    Yes. We wrap vehicles for businesses across the GTA, including Etobicoke, Mississauga, Brampton, and Vaughan, and throughout Ontario.

  7. What do you need from me to get started?

    A vector version of your logo, photos of your vehicle, and any design ideas you have. That’s enough for our team to begin a concept within 48 hours.
